terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here: its last line shows whether the shelf survived the day.

tasks.title: Plan a new scent
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/copies.js`, make `withScent(scents, scent)` return a new list: every scent of `scents`, in order, with `scent` added at the end. `scents` itself stays as it was.

Check calls `withScent` with lists of its own, an empty one included, then makes sure the list it handed in has not changed and that what came back is a new list, not that same one.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on making a copy.
Make a new list that holds every scent of `scents`.
Put the new scent at its end, and give the new list back.
Run the file: the last line should show the shelf without Pine.
hints: `push` changes the list it is called on. Called on `scents`, it changes the shelf of whoever called `withScent`.
The spread form `...scents` inside square brackets lays out every scent of the old list in a new one, and you can write more items after it.
The body is one line: `return [...scents, scent]`.

tasks.title: Pick the featured scents
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make `featured(scents, count)` return a new list of the first `count` scents of `scents`, in their order. When `scents` has fewer than `count`, all of them are featured. `scents` stays as it was.

Check calls `featured` with lists and counts of its own, a count of 0, a count larger than the list and an empty list included, then makes sure the list it handed in has not changed and that a new list came back.
nextSteps: Look up `slice` in the lesson: where it starts and where it stops.
Use `count` to say where to stop.
Run the file and try a count larger than the shelf.
hints: One list tool from the lesson cuts out a part of a list as a new list, without touching the old one.
`slice(start, end)` keeps the items from `start` up to, but not including, `end`. An `end` past the last item is no error: it just stops at the end, and it still makes a new list.
The body is one line: `return scents.slice(0, count)`.

tasks.title: Leave the last one out
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `withoutLast(scents)` return a new list of every scent of `scents` but the last one. An empty list gives an empty list. `scents` stays as it was.

Check calls `withoutLast` with lists of its own, one scent and none included, then makes sure the list it handed in has not changed and that a new list came back.
nextSteps: Remember what `pop` does to the list it is called on.
Make the new list with a tool that leaves the old one alone.
Work out where to stop from the length of `scents`.
Run the file: the shelf in the last line should still end in Amber.
hints: `pop` would take the last scent off the shelf of whoever called you. Use a tool that makes a new list instead.
`slice` stops just before its end position, so the end you want is the last position, worked out from the length. Or copy the list first and change only the copy.
The body is one line: `return scents.slice(0, scents.length - 1)`.

tasks.title: Label without touching the shelf
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, first write a function of your own, `labelFor(scent)`: it returns `'Wickhollow '` followed by the scent, like `'Wickhollow Sage'`. It only helps `labelsFor`, so it stays off the export line.

Then fix Theo's `labelsFor(scents)`. Today it writes the labels over the list it is given. Make it return a new list with the label of each scent, in the same order, using `labelFor`, and leave `scents` as it was.

Check calls `labelFor` with scents of its own, then `labelsFor` with lists of its own, an empty one included. It makes sure the list handed in has not changed, that a new list came back, and that `labelsFor` uses `labelFor`.
nextSteps: Run the file and read its last line: Theo's function changed the shelf.
Write `labelFor` above `labelsFor`, from its name to its closing brace.
In `labelsFor`, start an empty list and fill it, one label per scent.
Give the new list back and run the file again.
hints: `scents[i] = ...` puts a value at a position of the list it was handed, which is the shelf itself. The labels need a list of their own.
Start with an empty list before the loop, `push` one label into it for each scent, and give it back after the loop.
`labelFor` is `return 'Wickhollow ' + scent`. In `labelsFor`: `const labels = []`, then `for (const scent of scents) { labels.push(labelFor(scent)) }`, then `return labels`.
